title: fringe day one - 4 shows - 3 musicals - one stand up. 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 #edfrin...
transcript: I just got back from my very first Edinburgh Fringe and it was one of the coolest experiences of my entire life I saw 34 shows over the course of five days and I wanna talk a little bit about each show how I got the tickets how much I spent and what I thought let's start with day one I saw four shows cause we actually took the train up from London in the morning first show I saw at the fringe was ‘a history of paper’ which I was intentional about because it was a world premiere Scottish musical and I thought that felt like a very goodfirst fringe show it started appearing on Fringe List kind of early and it looked interesting so I grabbed a ticket and I'm really glad I did because by the time I got to fringe the entire run was sold out this was also the most expensive ticket I bought the entiretime at fringe it was £23 at traverse there's a lot I really liked about this show it is a very intimate two hander the story is a man going through this box of papers of receipts and cards and origami they document his relationship with this woman who he has presumably lost and as he goes through these papers you watch them fall in love and you see the entire outline of their relationship almost has like a last five years element to it there also like songs and monologues about the actual history of paper and like how paper came to be and I thought those moments are very cool and there's a huge twist that I did not love the people around me really really did and everybody was like weeping highlight of the show for me was without a doubt the music like I just loved the score and the richness of this soundtrack and they like only had a piano so I can't imagine this if it was like fully orchestrated you know not loving the twist is definitely a me thing but it was very effective and like worked in the story and I think the staging was stunning and I hope this gets further developed which they also got a fringe first award so it feels like a possibility next show I saw was Sophie Dukes but daddy I love her which was a stand up comedy show I didn't know Sophie before the fringe my friends wanted to go because they love the show taskmaster we bought these tickets I think it was like £12 I'm so glad I went because Sophie was hilarious and this ended up being the only stand up I saw the entire trip which funny because fringe just like known for stand up but daddy I love her is about Sophie and her relationship with her father I like scream laughed it was so funny but then there's also some really tender moments in the show Sophie like picks a man from the audience to be her dad for the show and she has him write her a message of support and then at the end of the show she had him read it out loud and it was like Sophie I'm so proud of you like I'm so happy of what you accomplished it was really sweet and I was like kind of tearing up it was a very lovely moment so I I really liked that but anyway I really only wanna see funny women and then we want to see Diva live from hell which I was invited to as an accredited member of the media I really knew nothing about this show going in and I was so surprised by how much fun it was the way I've been describing it is it's like if all about Eve mets sisyphus the man who had to push the rock up the hill forever it's a one person show set in a cabaret club in hell where Desmond played by Luke Bauer who's incredible is telling the story of what lead to his death and how he ended up burning in hell and he has to tell the story over and over and over again forever so campy it's filled with musical theater references it's just a delight it works so well on every single level for me last I saw diary of a gay disaster which I just went up to the box office and bought tickets there for like £12 and this show surprised me so much it was such a joy it's about three queer people who are literally stuck in a fever dream and they're using this diary to like relive their most like traumatic queer moments but it's hilarious the music is so good did not stop laughing from like the first moment until the end it was the most like fringy show of the day like it's literally just three people there like no sets no costumes but great music really good story and I cannot wait to see them develop this further also some of the best nonbinary rep I've like seen on stage like they really take the time to like dive into what it means to be nonbinary and I loved it and the three actors who were in it were all exceptionally talented vocalist it was just it was great all the way around A+ day one I loved all four of these that was definitely my smallest day of shows which is saying something
